back: Marketing goods or services to customers in more than one country, often with changes to the mix.

front: Methods of entering a foreign market
back: Exporting, licensing, franchising, joint venture and direct investment.
Low investment and risk, but transport cost, tariffs and exchange-rate risk and less control.
Shared ownership with a local partner: local knowledge and shared risk, but shared profit and control.
A standardised mix everywhere: lower cost and consistent image, but may ignore local tastes.
Changing the mix for each market: better fit with local tastes, but higher cost.

front: Factors in choosing a foreign market
back: Size, growth, income and tastes, competition, stability, trade barriers, distance and ease of entry.

front: Benefits and challenges of foreign markets
back: Benefits: more sales, spread risk, foreign income. Challenges: tastes, language, law, exchange rates, payment and distance.

front: Strategies for breaking into foreign markets
back: Start nearby, use a local agent or partner, adapt the product, use trade fairs and online sales, build trust with small orders.
